pr_body:
Fixes #1072 
Error logging is performed only if there is no customErrorHandler or if has already been called. This allows the customErrorHandler to process and/or rethrow custom errors that are not supported by the built-in function and that would be incorrectly logged.
Moreover in case of log.info the request is also printed.

- [x] tests and/or benchmarks are included
- [ ] documentation is changed or added
- [x] commit message and code follows [Code of conduct](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/master/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

issue_context.title: Thrown errors processed by the errorHandler are logged as 500 even if status code is altered
comments:
> Whether a reply.send(new CustomHTTPError()) or throw new CustomHTTPError() is used, the default logger always logs it at error level even if the error does not correspond to an internal error (e.g. NotFound or Unauthorized).

I think we should fix this. Would you like to send a PR?

I couldn't really follow the rest of the issue. What would be your expected output?

The main issue is that if you want to encapsulate HTTP errors in objects that do not have  `statusCode` they are always logged as error. (`statusCode` is required as per [docs](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/master/docs/Reply.md#errors))

In case an errorHandler function is provided that can process those objects and return the expected HTTP codes to the client the expected behaviour would be that codes >= 500 are still logged as error while codes >= 400 are logged as info. This is not the case as the error is logged before the errorHandler is called.

This is the current behaviour
1. throw boom.unauthorized()
2. log.error
3. errorHandler ( reply.code(401).send() )

Output:
```
[INFO] incoming request GET xxx /endpoint
[ERROR] Unauthorized GET 500 /endpoint
[INFO] request completed 1ms
```

This is what I would expect
1. throw boom.unauthorized()
2. errorHandler ( reply.code(401).send() )
3. log.info

Output:
```
[INFO] incoming request GET xxx /endpoint
[INFO] Unauthorized GET 401 /endpoint
[INFO] request completed 1ms
```

> The main issue is that if you want to encapsulate HTTP errors in objects that do not have statusCode they are always logged as error. (statusCode is required as per docs).

I would make this even stricter: if it's not an error, fastify should crash badly. We should use `Error` (or descendants) as errors, and not just random objects. Boom errors descend from `Error`, so I don't understand why this applies to this issue.

Would you like to send a PR to have it logged as INFO if `res.statusCode && res.statusCode !== 500`?

>Boom errors descend from Error, so I don't understand why this applies to this issue.

Boom errors have `statusCode` inside `output` property so `res.statusCode` is defaulted to 500.

https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/ea3f220261af85ffe62aa24151fea81a938b6daf/lib/reply.js#L266-L288

Moreover there is no check on the instance type. A simple object `{ statusCode: 401 }` is valid for `handleError` function.

> Would you like to send a PR to have it logged as INFO if res.statusCode && res.statusCode !== 500?

I can do it, but I think that:
1. errors should be logged after customErrorHandler returns (if defined, immediately otherwise) ([code](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/ea3f220261af85ffe62aa24151fea81a938b6daf/lib/reply.js#L290-L308))
2. `code >= 500` should be ERROR, `500 > code >= 400` should be INFO
3. errors without statusCode should be ERROR
4. log should contain req object so that it can be pointed to the original request ([code](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/ea3f220261af85ffe62aa24151fea81a938b6daf/lib/reply.js#L293))

> if it's not an error, fastify should crash badly

I agree. What's the best way to do it?

I agree on all the above.
Note that boom support was removed in https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/558/files#diff-d2fdf63c1d7f1d9f68270b6dfa8c930cL42.

I agree we should wait for the customErrorHandler to complete, and check the statusCode of the response instead of the one inside the error itself.

> > if it's not an error, fastify should crash badly

> I agree. What's the best way to do it?

In https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/master/lib/handleRequest.js#L84-L116. At least we should log a warning.

> Note that boom support was removed in https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/558/files#diff-d2fdf63c1d7f1d9f68270b6dfa8c930cL42.

Yep, that's the reason for fastify-boom.

> In https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/master/lib/handleRequest.js#L84-L116. At least we should log a warning.

I'm struggling on how to implement it. Something like this?
1. handleError: throw new Error()
2. handleRequest: catch error, log.fatal, reply.code(500).send(), process.exit(...)

I'd like to call `onClose` hook from `handleRequest` so that everything else (e.g. db connection) closes safely but I have no clue how to call it. maybe `this.close()`? (I read through the code but I'm not sure...)

> I'd like to call onClose hook from handleRequest so that everything else (e.g. db connection) closes safely but I have no clue how to call it. maybe this.close()? (I read through the code but I'm not sure...)

First let's resolve this issue about boom support, then let's do the other one.

review_comments: I'm not convinced here: log the request every time could be onerous. Or not?
This was just pre-existing behavior moved around, if you would like to discuss that open a new issue/p.
I'm not sure logging the response object is correct here. I can understand the request being logged, but I really think only the error needs to be logged.
